out_items.name: Food separated and protected

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal and RTE Foods
violations.observation: Raw animal food storage, preparation, holding or display conducted in a manner that may cause cross contamination of ready-to-eat food as follows: OBSERVED IN WALK-IN COOLER: RAW BEEF STORED ABOVE JALAPEÑO AND RAW CHICKEN STORED ABOVE PICKLED CABBAGE.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from cross contamination by separating raw animal foods like poultry, beef, pork, seafood, and eggs from cooked foods, ready-to- eat foods, washed produce, etc during storage, preparation, holding or display. Raw foods shall be stored on shelving units BELOW or SEPARATED from all cooked foods, commercially processed foods, washed produce, leftover foods, etc. CDI: RAW FOODS MOVED TO THE BOTTOM SHELVES DURING INSPECTION. PIC RE-EDUCATED.

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal Foods Different Types
violations.observation: Different types of raw animal foods stored in such a manner that may cause cross contamination as follows: OBSERVED IN WALK-IN COOLER: RAW BEEF STORED ABOVE RAW EGG
violations.corrective_action: Raw animal foods shall be sorted by their 'type' and cooking temperatures while in storage inside a refrigerator or freezer. For example, if using ONE shelving unit for storage of ONLY raw foods, the foods shall be sorted in this manner: 1) raw poultry (chicken, turkey, or duck) shall be stored on the BOTTOM shelf (165F cook temperature), 2) raw ground beef and ground pork shall be stored on the shelf above poultry (155F cook temperature), and 3) raw pork (chops, ribs), seafood, and shell eggs shall be stored on the top shelf above beef (145F cook temperature). CDI: RAW BEEF MOVED BELOW THE RAW SHELL EGGS.

out_items.name: Proper hot holding temperatures

violations.title: Hot Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed hot holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: OBSERVED COOKED RICE IN HOT CABINET AT 108F.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature conrol for safety food shall be held hot at a temperature of 135F or above unless the permit holder is using 'time as the public health control' as specified under 3-501.19. CDI: PIC CHOSE TO DISPOSE OF RICE INSTEAD OF REHEATING.

out_items.name: Compliance with variance, specialized process, HACCP

violations.title: Variance Requirement, Health Department Determines Need
violations.observation: Observed the facility was making traditional kimchi by keeping cabbage, vegetable soup and radishes outside of refrigeration for over 24 hours approximately two weeks to ferment kimchi. Observed fermented kimchi in the dry storage area next to dry storage shelving, observed temperatures of the kimchi in the containers was 68F and 69F. Date marking on kimchi containers was 12/29/25 .
violations.corrective_action: A food establishment shall obtain a variance from the Regulatory Authority as specified in 8-103.10 and under 8-103.11 before: 1. smoking food as a method of food preservation rather than as a method for flavor enhancement, 2. curing food, 3. using food additives or adding components such as vinegar, 4. packaging food using a Reduced Oxygen Packaging method, 5. operating a molluscan shellfish life-support system display tank used to store and display shellfish that are offered for human consumption, 6. custom processing animals that are for personal use as food and not for sale or service in a food establishment, 7. preparing food by another method that is determined by the Regularty Authority to require a variance or, 8. sprouting seeds or beans. EHS had PIC and employees dispose of kimchi. PIC and EHS agreed to no longer make traditional Kimchi until a HACCP plan can be filed with Health Department. Follow up to verify compliance will occur in 1 week.

out_items.name: Food properly labeled, original container

violations.title: Food Storage Container, Common Name
violations.observation: The following food items that are not easily identified by appearance were observed without a label: observe Tupperware’s full of salt, sugar, flour, MSG and various dry, use items being stored without proper common name labels
violations.corrective_action: Unless a food item can be easily recognized, all foods and ingredients removed from their original containers and stored in working containers shall be labeled using the common name of the food. For example: cooking oils, salt, sugar, flour, spices, herbs, etc. Person in charge had employee label food during time of inspection.

out_items.name: In-use utensils properly stored

violations.title: In-Use Utensils Proper Storage
violations.observation: Dispensing and/or in-use utensils improperly stored between use as follows: observed on the cook line multiple rice scoops being stored in containers full of non- heated non-running water
violations.corrective_action: During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food utensils shall be stored in one of the following manners: 1) in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container, 2) in food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed, 3) on a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized, 4) in running water of sufficient velocity to flush particulates to the drain, 5) in a clean, protected location if the utensils are used only with a food that is NOT TCS food, or 6) in a container of water if the water is maintained at a temperature of at least 135F and the container is cleaned frequently. Person in charge disposed of the water and had the rice scoops washed rinse and sanitized. CHOSUN HWARO (Inspection Date: 01/07/2026) Page 3 of 4
